shapes.html: We define system composition through single-step components.

notes: Here the same composition is shown at three levels of description. The middle is a single-step construction, its type is on the right, and run gives the behaviour over sequences on the left. These are not three abstraction-pyramid levels. Orient the audience; all four signatures are already visible.
Sequential composition takes g as its first function argument. Follow its input/output/state types and the highlighted g box. Function-argument order in this notation is not temporal execution order.
It also takes f. In the composed reaction, the output of f feeds the input of g. Distinguish the written g/f argument order from dataflow f to g.

The result is a new single-step component. Its input/output types describe the composed connection, and its state combines the two component state spaces. Follow the displayed tuple order; these are distinct state resources, not arbitrary shared-state aliases.

The pass-through and parallel constructions follow the same principle. Their single-step composition lifts to the expected synchronous behaviour; the signal-pairing isomorphism gives the correspondence between separate streams and tuples. Do not reread all four types. This relies on the established lifting and component behaviours (thesis Propositions 3.2–3.3 and Corollary 3.4), not well-typedness alone proving arbitrary functional equivalence. Parallel branches do not prescribe a physical schedule. Next: We can now compose components with distinct state spaces. We need to account for feedback and components that share state.
